name: Question 8
problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,2t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\times ⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27{cos}^{2}⁡3t-27{sin}^{2}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27⟩ \\  & =9⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-3⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡3t+9{sin}^{2}⁡3t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4} \\  & =\sqrt{13}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =9\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3)}^{2}} \\  & =9\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡3t+4{sin}^{2}⁡3t+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨sin⁡3t,cos⁡3t,2t⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
3
b
313
c
9
d
913
e
1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(sin⁡3t),ddt(cos⁡3t),ddt(2t)⟩=⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,2⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(3cos⁡3t),ddt(−3sin⁡3t),ddt(2)⟩=⟨−9sin⁡3t,−9cos⁡3t,0⟩

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,2⟩×⟨−9sin⁡3t,−9cos⁡3t,0⟩=ijk3cos⁡3t−3sin⁡3t2−9sin⁡3t−9cos⁡3t0= −3sin⁡3t2−9cos⁡3t0i−3cos⁡3t2−9sin⁡3t0j+3cos⁡3t−3sin⁡3t−9sin⁡3t−9cos⁡3tk=⟨18cos⁡3t,−18sin⁡3t,−27cos2⁡3t−27sin2⁡3t⟩=⟨18cos⁡3t,−18sin⁡3t,−27⟩=9⟨2cos⁡3t,−2sin⁡3t,−3⟩,||v||=(3cos⁡3t)2+(−3sin⁡3t)2+(2)2=9cos2⁡3t+9sin2⁡3t+4=9(cos2⁡3t+sin2⁡3t)+4=9+4=13,||v×a||=9(2cos⁡3t)2+(−2sin⁡3t)2+(−3)2=94cos2⁡3t+4sin2⁡3t+9=94(cos2⁡3t+sin2⁡3t)+9=94+9=913

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get aN=||v×a||||v||=91313=9.
